transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Honestly, what finally pushed me to come in is how tense my body is all the time. My shoulders and neck just stay clenched through the day, like I’m bracing for a classroom observation that never ends. By the evening my jaw aches so much that I can barely enjoy playing guitar.
Does the jaw ache stay in one place or does it spread to other areas of your face or head?
I’m not really sure. I notice it mostly right in my jaw, kind of around the hinges, but I haven’t paid close attention to whether it spreads into my head or face.
Is the jaw ache present all the time or does it come and go?

It kind of builds through the day. The shoulder and neck clenching feels pretty constant, like I’m tense all day, but the jaw ache is worst by evening—bad enough that it gets in the way of playing guitar.
Is the tension in your shoulders and neck worse when you're at work or thinking about work?

It’s there pretty much all day, but yeah, it does feel tied to work. I’m a teacher, and it’s like my shoulders and neck stay clenched like I’m constantly being observed in the classroom, even when nothing is actually happening. By the evening it’s really worn me down.
Are there any particular situations at work that make your shoulder and neck tension worse?

Honestly, it’s less one specific situation and more this constant feeling like I’m bracing for someone watching or evaluating me in the classroom. My shoulders and neck just stay clenched through the day, like an observation that never ends. By the evening it’s bad enough that my jaw aches and I can barely enjoy playing guitar.
Have you experienced any significant stress or anxiety outside of work that you think might be contributing to your tension?

Yes. It’s not only work in the moment. My mind keeps going around and around about bigger things—like whether I’ll ever get hired again, or whether I’ve damaged my reputation with parents. Then it jumps to retirement, like I’m running out of time. And sometimes I’ll fixate on something small, like a mistake during story time, and start thinking maybe it means I shouldn’t be trusted with children. It’s hard to shut off.
Are you having trouble sleeping because of these thoughts or tension?

Yes. Most nights I get into bed and my mind just starts going—replaying interview answers, thinking about bills, licensing forms, all of it. I can be lying there for hours. And even when I do fall asleep, I often wake up around four in the morning already tense, already calculating what could go wrong that day.
Have you ever had a sudden episode of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve had something that suddenly peaks like that within minutes. Mine feels more like it builds and stays there, if that makes sense.
Do you find it difficult to control your worry about work, finances, or other things?

Yes, very difficult. I try to stop it—I’ll tell myself, “Make a list,” or “Just focus on the next step.” Sometimes I’ll pray or go out and weed the garden to get my mind off it. But it doesn’t really stop. One worry just turns into the next one, and before I know it I’ve lost half the afternoon going over things in my head.
Have you been avoiding social situations or activities you normally enjoy because of your tension or worries?

Yes. I’ve pulled back from things I’d normally do. I used to volunteer for story-time, but now I won’t really do it unless someone else handles the planning, because I get too worked up about all the details. And with trying to get back into the classroom, it’s been a real problem—I’ve missed application deadlines and stumbled through interviews because I’m so tense and worried. It’s keeping me from being reliable with it.
Is the pain in your jaw, shoulders, or neck constant, or are there times when you don't feel it at all?

It’s pretty constant, honestly. My shoulders and neck feel clenched most of the day, like I’m bracing for something that never lets up. By evening my jaw aches too, and sometimes it’s bad enough that I don’t even enjoy playing guitar.
Are you finding it hard to do everyday tasks because of how you've been feeling?

Yes. It’s gotten in the way of basic things I need to follow through on. I’ve missed application deadlines, and when I do get an interview, I feel so worked up that I stumble through it. I’ve also stopped volunteering for story-time unless someone else is handling the planning. So it’s making it hard for me to get back into the classroom in any steady, reliable way.
Are there any physical activities you've stopped doing altogether because of the tension or pain in your jaw, shoulders, or neck?

I haven’t stopped everything, but guitar is the big one. By the evening my jaw is aching and my shoulders and neck are still so clenched that I can hardly enjoy playing. That’s actually part of what pushed me to come in—it just feels like I’m bracing all day and can’t really let down.
Do you notice that your jaw, shoulder, or neck pain gets worse when you're worrying about something specific?

Yes, definitely. When I’m worried about something—especially anything that feels like being judged or observed—my shoulders and neck just lock up. It feels like I’m bracing for a classroom observation that never ends. By the end of the day my jaw aches too, and sometimes it’s bad enough that I can hardly enjoy playing guitar.
Are your relationships with family or friends being affected by how you've been feeling?

I’m not sure. I mean, I haven’t really noticed a clear problem with family or friends specifically. I think I’ve been more wrapped up in my own head, but I can’t say it’s directly changed those relationships in a way I can point to.
Have you felt like your tension, worries, or pain have made it hard for you to take care of yourself or your daily responsibilities?

Yes. It’s gotten in the way pretty badly. I’ve missed application deadlines, and when I do get to interviews, I feel like I stumble through them. I also stopped volunteering for story-time unless someone else does the planning part. So… it’s keeping me from getting back into the classroom in any reliable way.
Do you think your body tension and pain are related to your worries and fears?

Yes, I do. It really feels connected. When I’m worried or afraid, my shoulders and neck stay tight all day, like I’m bracing for something. By evening my jaw is aching, and sometimes it’s bad enough that I don’t even enjoy playing guitar.
Do you think the tension in your body is a physical expression of your worries?

Yes. That’s how it feels to me. My shoulders and neck are clenched almost all day, like I’m bracing for something that never actually happens. By the evening my jaw hurts so much that even playing guitar isn’t really enjoyable.
Do you think your jaw, shoulder, or neck pain would improve if your worries and fears were resolved?

Yes, I think it probably would. The tension feels tied to the worrying. My shoulders and neck are clenched all day, like I’m bracing for something, and by evening my jaw aches so much I can barely enjoy playing guitar. So if the fear and worry eased up, I do think the pain would ease too.
